title: Class IV haemorrhage, PEA and resuscitation (phases)
story: A 35-year-old man bleeding 2.5 L over 10 minutes, breathing room air: oxygen and the ventilator come only from your steps. The bleed ends at 10 minutes: that is the surgeon's source control. Intubated and ventilated, positive pressure cuts the venous return of an empty patient and he loses his pulse at about 11 minutes on a junctional rhythm (PEA). Start CPR at once, with massive transfusion (1 L crystalloid, then red cells and plasma by rapid infuser), tranexamic acid and epinephrine every 3–5 minutes: compressions and volume restore the coronary perfusion pressure, and the circulation comes back from the PEA, which you recognise at a rhythm check on the arterial line and the capnogram. Left untreated, the PEA decays into asystole about 4½ minutes after the pulse loss, and in this model a heart in asystole does not regain its pulse: the time to CPR decides the case. Nothing on this card sets VF: the physiology does not produce it on this course.
takeHome: Positive pressure and induction can tip a compensated bleeding patient into arrest.
In haemorrhagic arrest, stopping the bleeding and giving blood come first; compressions cannot fill an empty heart.
EtCO₂ and the arterial diastolic pressure show how good the CPR is, and they show the return of circulation.
notes: pme-scenario/2 translation of showcase-haemorrhage (plan F9; design §4.2 and §11; the owner's rulings of 5 November). PHASES are the course, each entered by its own rule on engine truth, none by a button: Bleeding (start; the card-set 2.5 L bleed over 10 min), Decompensating (systolic below 60 for 10 s, the /1 card's own rule; the card sets a junctional rhythm at 50/min on its entry, as the /1 card does), Arrest PEA and Arrest asystole (the model's pulse loss, told apart by the rhythm id the engine draws: asystole, or any other), ROSC (the model's return of circulation) and Post-resuscitation (ROSC held 120 s, design §4.2). NO VF PHASE: the owner's ruling of 5 November (VF comes from the physiology, never from a press) and its measurement on this card's course (the PR of plan F9): the engine draws no VF on this course untreated (to 30:00), with CPR into asystole (the demo's timing) or with CPR in the PEA; the /1 card's scripted VF at the first two rhythm checks is gone, and with it the shocks. The rhythm check is an action: it stops the compressions for the check and does nothing to the rhythm. ACTIONS are the team's, each with its criteria and, in its src, the source of its numbers quoted and cited (the owner's ruling of 5 November, 'guideline for all'); an action whose sources state no window is recorded, not timed. The engine receives the /1 card's commands for the same presses (the press gives are the /1 states' onEnter commands), except the scripted VF and what follows from it.

phases.label: Bleeding
phases.notes: Bleeding 2.5 L over 10 min, breathing room air: oxygen and the ventilator come only from your steps.

phases.label: Decompensating
phases.$comment: The /1 card's rule from its ventilated state (systolic below 60 for 10 s), read on truth. The /1 card also let a button force the junctional rhythm; a phase is never entered by a button (design §4, plan Q5), so that press is gone.
phases.notes: The card sets the rhythm: a junctional rhythm at 50/min (an instructor rhythm event, not the physiology). The pulse loss that follows is the model's.

phases.label: Arrest: PEA
phases.$comment: The model's pulse loss on an organised rhythm (the running junctional rhythm, then its slow idioventricular decay: the engine's 'agonal'). No hold: a pulseless patient is shown pulseless at once (the MH card's D4). No VF is told apart: the engine draws none on this course (the measurement in the F9 PR).
phases.notes: The model's PEA on the running junctional rhythm: the arterial line first reads about 20/14 (pseudo-PEA: a pressure too low to feel), then goes flat. On the owner's course it is left untreated: it slows, becomes idioventricular and turns to asystole about 5 minutes after the pulse loss.

phases.label: Arrest: asystole
phases.notes: The untreated PEA has decayed to asystole. In this model asystole stays: compressions and volume no longer bring the pulse back (the engine's ROSC is that of an organised rhythm).

phases.label: ROSC
phases.notes: The pulse is back: CPR and volume have held the coronary perfusion pressure (at least 15 mmHg) and the myocardium for 60 s. Recognise it at the rhythm check on the arterial line and the capnogram, then stop CPR.

phases.label: Post-resuscitation
phases.$comment: ROSC held 120 s (design §4.2): the rule is the return of circulation, held without a break for 120 s from ROSC's entry.

actions.label: Oxygen by face mask, FiO₂ 1.0
actions.$comment: Graded as done in Bleeding or Decompensating (no window: see src).
actions.src: No window: none is stated in the sources read (owner's ruling of 5 November: recorded, not timed: no window is stated in the sources read); graded as done in Bleeding or Decompensating.

actions.label: Intubate and ventilate, FiO₂ 1.0
actions.$comment: Graded as done in Bleeding or Decompensating (no window: see src). Positive pressure then takes the empty patient into arrest: the lesson needs no phase (design §4.2).
actions.src: No window: none is stated in the sources read (recorded, not timed: no window is stated in the sources read); graded as done in Bleeding or Decompensating.

actions.label: Call for help
actions.$comment: The owner's ruling of 5 November: an action the instructor presses when the team calls. No engine command: the press is recorded by the scenario record command. No window (see src): graded as done in its phases.
actions.src: No window: no source reachable states one (recorded, not timed: no window is stated in the sources read); graded as done in its phases.

actions.label: Start CPR: compressions 100–120/min, bag via the tube 10/min, FiO₂ 1.0
actions.$comment: The /1 card's objective 2 (CPR within 30 s of the model's pulse loss) and the owner's ruling of 5 November: within 30 s met, 30 s to 2 min overdue, after 2 min failed though started (failAfterS). Rate 100–120/min (design §11). Press it again to resume the compressions after a rhythm check.
actions.src: Window: the /1 card's objective 2 (within 30 s of the pulse loss); fail limit 120 s: the owner's ruling of 5 November; rate 100–120/min: design §11. Resuming after a rhythm check (the CPR press again) is recorded, not timed: no window is stated in the sources read: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (2025), Ch82 'Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Advanced Cardiac Life Support' (AHA-based; the source the owner's 'guideline for all' ruling takes, 5 November, until the ERC 2021 text is in the library), PDF p.3: 'the compressions should be resumed as soon as possible after rhythm analysis or defibrillation.'

actions.label: Bag via the tube 10/min, FiO₂ 1.0
actions.$comment: Design §11 (bag 10/min); graded on the bag-valve ventilation whatever sent it (the CPR press sends it).
actions.src: 10/min: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (2025), Ch82 'Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Advanced Cardiac Life Support' (AHA-based; the source the owner's 'guideline for all' ruling takes, 5 November, until the ERC 2021 text is in the library), PDF p.7: 'After placement of an advanced airway, it is recommended to provide 1 breath every 6 seconds (10 breaths/min) while continuous chest compressions are being performed.' No window (recorded, not timed: no window is stated in the sources read).

actions.label: Epinephrine 1 mg IV
actions.$comment: Design §11: epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 min, each repeat from the previous dose as given (the owner's ruling of 5 November). The violation: epinephrine 1 mg IV or IO after the return of circulation (design §7).

contraindications.text: Epinephrine 1 mg IV or IO after the return of circulation: the arrest dose into a beating heart

actions.src: Repeat 180–300 s from the previous dose as given: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (2025), Ch82 'Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Advanced Cardiac Life Support' (AHA-based; the source the owner's 'guideline for all' ruling takes, 5 November, until the ERC 2021 text is in the library), PDF p.9: 'standard-dose epinephrine (1 mg every 3–5 minutes) is recommended for patients in cardiac arrest.' The first dose has no window (recorded, not timed: no window is stated in the sources read). Violation IV or IO: the owner's ruling of 5 November.

actions.label: Surgeon controls the bleeding
actions.$comment: Design §11. The bleed rate goes to 0 (the 2.5 L bleed has already ended at 10:00 on this course).
actions.src: No window (recorded, not timed: no window is stated in the sources read); offered in the arrest phases, as on the /1 card.

actions.label: Massive transfusion: 1 L warmed crystalloid, then red cells and plasma by rapid infuser
actions.$comment: The press gives the /1 card's 1 L balanced crystalloid over 90 s and 1200 mL of the engine's whole blood over 144 s (500 mL/min). The crystalloid enters at the theatre's 21 °C (no fluid warmer in the scenario schema).
actions.src: Blood at ≥ 300 mL/min: the plan's criterion (scenario-format-v2-plan.md §F9). Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed., Ch45, Ch46 and Ch62 were read and define no massive-transfusion volume or rate; the nearest statements: Ch45 Fig. 45.7 (PDF p.23, printed p.1420), indications for the transfusion protocol 'BP <90 mm Hg after 2 PRBC' and 'Blood loss = circulating blood volume'; Ch62 Fig. 62.9 (PDF p.21, printed p.2020), activation in the trauma OR at 'EBL > 150 mL/min'. No window (recorded, not timed: no window is stated in the sources read).

actions.label: Tranexamic acid 1 g IV
actions.$comment: Design §11: TXA 1 g IV. Logged: no effect on the monitor until a coagulation model exists.
actions.src: 1 g: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed., Ch62 Fig. 62.9 (PDF p.21, printed p.2020): 'Consider tranexamic acid 1 g over 10 minutes followed by infusion of 1 g over 8 hours'. No window (recorded, not timed: no window is stated in the sources read); the 3-h clause dropped (CRASH-2's window is always satisfied in this 25-min case).

actions.label: Rhythm check (compressions pause)
actions.$comment: Design §11: a rhythm check every 2 min (the values and their source: src). The owner's ruling of 5 November: it stops CPR for the check and does nothing to the rhythm (no card-set VF). Resume the compressions with the CPR press.
actions.src: Every 2 min: Miller's Anesthesia, 10th ed. (2025), Ch82 'Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation and Advanced Cardiac Life Support' (AHA-based; the source the owner's 'guideline for all' ruling takes, 5 November, until the ERC 2021 text is in the library), PDF p.9: compressions 'continued for 2 minutes before reassessing the underlying cardiac rhythm'. Tolerance ±10 s: the 10 s is the pulse-check pause limit, PDF p.3 ('The health care provider should take no more than 10 seconds to check for a pulse'), applied by the orchestrator as the interval tolerance (5 November); the text states no tolerance for the interval. First check 110–130 s after CPR starts, then every 110–130 s from the previous check as taken.

actions.label: Rhythm check: pulse back, stop CPR
actions.$comment: The /1 card's objective 3: stop CPR within 120 s of the model's return of circulation. The press gives the /1 card's rosc state: compressions off, the ventilator back at 12 × 500, PEEP 5, FiO₂ 1.0.
actions.src: Within 120 s of ROSC: the /1 card's objective 3.

judged.text: Recognise PEA from hypovolaemia: a rhythm on the ECG with no palpable pulse (pseudo-PEA at ART about 20/14: name it)
judged.$comment: The /1 card's objective 1. The clock starts on the displayed arterial systolic below 25 mmHg for 10 s, the /1 card's own PEA state (pseudo-PEA: ART about 20/14), what the learners see.

judged.text: Recognise the return of circulation on the arterial line and the capnogram at the rhythm check
judged.$comment: The /1 card's objective 3, its recognition half (the stop-CPR half is the action stopCpr). The clock starts at ROSC's entry, when the strip shows it.

script.$comment: The /1 card's bleeding state: 2.5 L over 10 min from the start.
The /1 card's junctional state: the card sets a junctional rhythm at 50/min (an instructor rhythm event, not the physiology). The pulse loss that follows is the model's.
